beats.text: If we split the world's income equally, people in rich countries would live on a third.
The world produces about twenty-six thousand dollars per person a year.
Each bar is one country's income per person. The line is the world average.
America and Germany sit about three times above it. India and Nigeria far below.
Split equally, everyone would live like an average person in Mexico or Thailand today.
Rich countries would take a pay cut. Most of the world would get a raise.

sources: IMF World Economic Outlook (2025), GDP per capita, PPP (current international $), 2025 estimates – world ≈ 25,600; USA ≈ 86,000; Germany ≈ 74,000; China ≈ 27,000; Mexico ≈ 26,000; Thailand ≈ 25,000; India ≈ 11,000; Nigeria ≈ 9,000 (rounded; editions differ by a few %). GDP per person is used as 'income per person' (standard proxy, e.g. Our World in Data); it is not take-home pay. 'Live like an average person in Mexico or Thailand' = same average output per person, ignoring distribution within countries.
